column1: # UNGRADABLE.tsv -- arizona_tests: shipped programs that CANNOT be graded as standalone programs, each named
# with the reason MEASURED against the oracle. THE PACKAGE LOCKDOWN (Lon 2026-09-06).
# Columns: path <TAB> REASON <TAB> evidence (the oracle's own words + how it was measured).
# Paths are relative to this package root: the suite ships TWO subdirectories, so a bare basename is ambiguous.
# ORACLE: icont/iconx 9.5.25a, /home/resources/icon-master/bin. CONTRACT: upstream's own tests/general/Test-icon --
#   icont -s NAME.icn ; ./NAME (or ./NAME.exe) < NAME.dat-if-present-else-/dev/null > out 2>&1 ; diff NAME.std out
# Determinism is two runs ONE SECOND APART, never back-to-back: a back-to-back pair cannot detect clock dependence
# (env.icn passes a back-to-back check and fails a 1s-apart one -- measured 2026-09-06 by hq_I).
# ✅⭐ THE WHOLE-SUITE ORACLE RE-READ, 2026-09-09 (hq_P, ceo CEO-452, the same method applied to jcon_tests):
# every one of the 90 shipped .std files was re-cut from the LIVE Arizona icont -- icont -s -o NAME NAME.icn,
# then NAME < NAME.dat-if-present-else-/dev/null > out 2>&1, determinism checked as two runs ONE SECOND APART
# per this header's own env.icn rule -- and ALL 90 AGREE BYTE FOR BYTE. Zero refused by the oracle, zero
# non-terminating, zero nondeterministic, zero cut by another implementation. ⛔ THIS SUITE NEEDS NO RE-CUT,
# which is worth writing down because the sister package did: jcon_tests carried 17 disagreements and 16 of
# its .std were cut by jcon, one of them announcing "&version: Jcon Version 2.2".
# ⚠ AND THE ONE TRAP THE CENSUS HIT, because it is the same class as jcon's io and it reads as an oracle
# disagreement: staged into a per-program directory, fncs1, io and recent showed 201, 3 and 137 differing
# lines. All three read files that live BESIDE them -- fncs1 opens gc1.icn, recent opens concord.dat, io
# lists and pipes its own companions including io.std. Re-run with the package directory intact, all three
# diff to ZERO. ⭐ test_icon_arizona_suite.sh is right to `cd "$SUITE"` and run in place; a future isolating
# rewrite of it would manufacture exactly these three failures and they would look like I/O defects.
# ⛔ These stay IN the denominator (POPULATION LAW 2026-09-04): shipped, never graded, never counted as passed.
# ⛔ "The oracle refuses it" is NOT written where OUR OWN vendoring edit is what the oracle refuses -- those rows
#    say so and name the control (upstream's unmodified file compiles; see FINDING-2026-09-06-hq_I-...).
general/features.icn
column3: Not a graded test: upstream tests/general/Test-icon runs it as a BANNER (`$IC -s features.icn -x`) to report the interpreter enabled build features, and never diffs it -- which is why upstream ships no features.std. Its output enumerates the ORACLE build (co-expressions, dynamic loading, external values, keyboard functions, large integers, pipes, system function); a different implementation legitimately prints a different set. ⛔⭐ THE PRECEDENT THIS ROW SETS WAS READ BACKWARDS ONCE AND THE ceo OVERTURNED IT HIMSELF (CEO-542, 2026-09-10, reversing CEO-527 on this row's own evidence): the gap between icont's list and ours -- TEN lines against our EIGHT, the difference being exactly `dynamic loading` and `external values` -- is US LACKING A FEATURE THE ORACLE HAS. That is OUR GAP, not the oracle's private contract, and this row is EVIDENCE FOR IT rather than a reason to stop grading anything. The fact that settles it: the C sources ship PUBLIC-DOMAIN in icon-master/ipl/cfuncs with lib/icall.h, so the library can be built against OUR header and OUR descriptor layout -- passing general/cfuncs and general/extlvals never required binary compatibility with iconx's internals, which was the whole basis of the withdrawn ruling. Those two are back IN the graded denominator, red, with their measured diffs. ⭐ WHAT IS STILL TRUE OF *THIS* FILE, and it is a different fact from the withdrawn one: features.icn IS NOT IN THE GRADED DENOMINATOR AT ALL, and never was -- the runner grades `for std in $SUITE/*.std` and UPSTREAM SHIPS NO features.std, because Test-icon runs it as a banner and never diffs it. So there is no exclusion here to un-land; putting it in the denominator would mean MINTING a ref upstream deliberately never cut. That is a ruling to make on purpose, not a revert -- and ⛔ THE ceo HAS NOW MADE IT: CEO-548 (2026-09-11) rules DO NOT MINT A REF UPSTREAM NEVER CUT. Cutting one here would manufacture a denominator entry upstream itself declines to grade, and it would be PERMANENTLY red by exactly the two feature words -- a standing red teaches its reader to ignore it, which costs more than the line it buys. features.icn stays ungraded, named here, out of the denominator and never hidden.
